newsitem.title: UK: NFC says market conditions remain tough.
newsitem.headline: NFC says market conditions remain tough.

text.p: Britain's NFC Plc, the distribution group, warned on Wednesday that market conditions remained challenging, particularly in Europe, but the board said it was still well placed to exploit future growth opportunities.

The outlook was given in the final results which showed pre-tax pre-exceptional profits up to 105.7 million stg from 76.2 million. The figures were bang in line with analysts' forecasts. The dividend payout for the year was flat at 7.1 pence per share. Turnover rose to 2.46 billion from 2.20 billion stg.
After recent restructuring efforts, expected to be completed in the current financial year, NFC said it was capable of making further progress.

Looking at the UK and Ireland division, sales were up 12 percent at 1.2 billion stg, with profits up 28 percent to 78.3 million. Strong business areas included the automotive business and TankFreight, but truck rental was described as less satisfactory.
The grocery industry business turned in better profits, but margins of some contracts remained pressured, it said. This area of business accounts for 14 percent of divisional revenue.
Continental Europe saw sales up 22 percent to 373.4 million stg, producing a loss of 8.5 million stg versus a 10.1 million loss last year.
The European logistics unit saw sales up 14 percent and a narrowing of losses by three percent. The German loss was flat after staff cuts and a withdrawal from frozen food delivery.

But the French chill network business was "disappointing" with a worsening of market conditions during the year and fuel price rises also hitting costs. The nationwide drivers' strike since the end of its financial year on September 30 has cost NFC 500,000 stg and hit margins.
But the Spanish and Portuguese markets were more robust with all divisions making "significant strides forward."
North American sales were up seven percent to 767.2 million, with profits up 73 percent to 25.5 million.
Excel Logistics sales were boosted by new business plus increased volumes from existing customers. The Kuhn Transportation acquisition also flattered the figures.
Other international operations saw sales up 16 percent to 111.7 million, with profits up 40 eprcent to six million.

The group is establishing an Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore. "This action anticipates significant growth opportunities as existing group customers in Europe and North America increase their sourcing and marketing activities in Asi-Pacific," said NFC in a statement.
